consumer_sentence: moved_during_run is unstamped, never FAIL: a settle-time consumer must read the record's `verdict` (and its before/after digests), not the process status -- exit 13 means the bytes it judged no longer exist, so the remedy is a re-run against the settled tree, never a FAIL stamp.
contract_decision: Creation cannot be DECLARED: `freeze` refuses a path that does not exist (exit 2) BEFORE the command runs, so a baseline of nothing never exists. Creation is WITNESSED instead: --wrap scans each declared root (parent dir of the declared paths, recursively, skipping .git/__pycache__/caches) before and after, emits `created` rows (before null, after sha), and prints that the declared set did not cover them. Document and test state the same rule; verify() (static, no scan) keeps its three states.
verdict_mapping: classify_verdict(exit_code, changed): 0+none=pass/0; 0+any=moved_during_run/13; nonzero+none=failed/1; nonzero+any=failed_and_moved/1 (record keeps the command's own exit_code). No fifth outcome.
unverified: any external (outside-repo) consumer of the wrapper or of exit 13 -- none exists in-repo to exercise
the declared-root scan cost on a very large declared root (bounded, recursive, cache dirs skipped, but not benchmarked here)
symlink retargeting and directory arguments are still outside the contract (unchanged by this card)
assumptions: classify(before) plus a before/after root scan is the intended reading of 'absent before, present after is a new file', since a declared path cannot be absent before the run without losing the baseline

keeping the CLI code 1 (not the command's own code) for failed/failed_and_moved preserves the tested contract while the record carries the command's own exit_code; the task's '(command's own exit)' is recorded in the record, not in the process status
next_unit_hint: Follow-up card (not this one): wire a settle-time consumer that reads the record's `verdict`/`deleted`/`created` and treats moved_during_run as unstamped.
